_comment: Hand-written inputs of the Gale site package (session B). Everything here is either a decision by the team or text with its source. build_site.py reads it.
name: Gale crater boxwork

habitat.status: team proposal (DATA.md, decision 3); build_site.py takes it from --habitat

usgs.credit: Parker and Calef (2016), MSL Gale Merged DEM 1m v3, USGS Astrogeology; HiRISE images NASA/JPL/University of Arizona

marstrek.credit: NASA/JPL Mars Trek, MRO HiRISE Gale Crater DEM 1 m; HiRISE images NASA/JPL/University of Arizona

ortho.credit: Calef and Parker (2016), MSL Gale Merged Orthophoto Mosaic v3, USGS Astrogeology; HiRISE images NASA/JPL/University of Arizona

sand_none.instrument: Not mapped (the 1 m elevation misses the hollows)
sand_none.credit: Checked by Walkback against the HiRISE 25 cm photo; plan B of the team's plan

sand.id: hollow = more than 0.5 m below the mean of the surrounding 20 m
sand.credit: Calculated by Walkback from the elevation; sandy hollows between the ridges: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS, PIA26696

globe_nasa3d.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech; Viking images processed at the USGS

globe_mdim.resolution: 1 km per pixel, shown at 4096 x 2048

stops.name: Altadena
stops.science: Curiosity's 43rd drill hole, in the boxwork bedrock: its powder went to the CheMin and SAM labs.
stops.scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4568-4569 (planning date 11 Jun 2025): Altadena drill hole imaged on sol 4564 (8 Jun 2025), sample delivered to CheMin and SAM, '42 drill sites that came before'
stops.taskSource: Task times proposed by the team; NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30, gives Apollo station-task statistics to compare with (same set as Valle de la Luna)
stops.risk: Gentle bedrock, slopes under 8° around it: the closest stop, 200 m from the habitat.
stops.tagSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4568-4569: drill hole image of 8 Jun 2025 (sol 4564)
stops.positionSource: Rover waypoint of sol 4560, where it stayed until sol 4571 (drill imaged sol 4564, campaign ending sols 4568-4569)
stops.riskSource: Slope and distance from the site's own elevation and site.json

stops.name: Valle de la Luna
stops.science: Curiosity's 44th drill hole, in the Monte Grande hollow: is the hollow rock different from the ridges?
stops.scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4695-4701 (13 Nov 2025): drill hole 44 inside the Monte Grande hollow
stops.taskSource: Task times proposed by the team; NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30, gives Apollo station-task statistics to compare with
stops.risk: Floor of a hollow, 2 m below the ridge next to it; edges up to 18° slope.
stops.tagSource: Drill sols from the NASA Curiosity blog; Earth dates from the REMS feed (sol 4693 = 2025-10-19, sol 4718 = 2025-11-13)

stops.name: Nevado Sajama
stops.science: Drilled on a boxwork ridge top, 10 m from Valle de la Luna: ridge rock versus hollow rock.
stops.scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4716-4722 (18 Nov 2025): drilled on top of a ridge, Navcam sol 4718
stops.nameOrigin: NASA named the target after an extinct volcano, the highest peak in Bolivia
stops.taskSource: Task times proposed by the team; NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30, gives Apollo station-task statistics to compare with
stops.risk: Ridge top, 2 m above the hollow; slopes up to 18° on the way up.
stops.tagSource: Drill sols from the NASA Curiosity blog; Earth dates from the REMS feed (sol 4693 = 2025-10-19, sol 4718 = 2025-11-13)

stops.name: Campo Marte
stops.science: Drill hole in the layered sulfate unit just above the boxwork; ChemCam and APXS measured it first.
stops.scienceSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4893-4899 (planning date 15 May 2026): same stratum as Atacama, 'the layered sulfate unit above the boxwork structures'; sols 4900-4907: first colour look of the drill hole, 16 May 2026 (sol 4897)
stops.nameOrigin: NASA named it after a natural red sandstone feature in Bolivia: 'Field of Mars'
stops.taskSource: Task times proposed by the team; NASA/TP-2017-219457, table 30, gives Apollo station-task statistics to compare with (same set as Valle de la Luna)
stops.risk: Loose blocks: next door at Atacama the drilled rock came up with the drill. 77 m above the habitat.
stops.tagSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4900-4907: drill hole image of 16 May 2026 (sol 4897)
stops.positionSource: Rover waypoint of sol 4893, where it stayed until sol 4912 (drilling sols 4895-4897). Proposed by a Fable 5.2 audit, checked against the waypoints and the blog
stops.riskSource: NASA Curiosity blog, sols 4900-4907: 'the rover picking up the entire Atacama block along with the drill'; height from the site's own elevation

photoTint.source: Median ground colour of Curiosity's Mastcam 360-degree mosaic at Nevado Sajama (PIA26696, NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS), 504 807 ground pixels below the horizon (data-pipeline/photo_tint.py); the HiRISE orthophoto mosaic is black and white
